title: Clean Contracts at a Host Call
statement: Let $M_0,\ldots,M_4$ be five finite Boolean Turing machines, and suppose their tape counts are all at most $K$. Fix an index $i$, maps $f,g$ from Boolean words to Boolean words, and a time-bound function $B$. If $M_i$ has positive tape count and, for every input word $x$ and argument word $\mathrm{arg}$, halts for the first time at some positive time $t\le B(|\mathrm{arg}|)$ with canonical seam containing $f(\mathrm{arg})$ and output $g(\mathrm{arg})$, then for every output prefix $\mathrm{pre}$ the host started at module $i$'s entry with argument $\mathrm{arg}$ avoids the loop anchor before such a time and reaches its resolved return with tape word $f(\mathrm{arg})$ and output $\mathrm{pre}$ followed by $g(\mathrm{arg})$.
hypotheses_covered: Five Boolean finite Turing machines indexed by $\mathrm{Fin}(5)$
A shared tape bound $K$ with $(M_j).k\le K$ for every $j$
replaced: If the module at index $i$ of the host satisfies the uniform clean contract for result map $f$, emission map $g$, and budget $B$, then from the host entry of $i$ over any argument and output prefix, the host reaches, within $B$ of the argument length and without touching the loop anchor, the resolved return over $f$ of the argument with the output extended by exactly $g$ of the argument.
